parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, facility ban, custody rule, border screening or documented current police targeting is shown, and same-sex conduct was decriminalised in 2022 by a functioning constitutional court. However, if outed the visitor has no statutory remedy for discrimination or harassment, which remain lawful, civil society reports no tangible implementation of the equality policy and that LGBTQ+ people avoid law enforcement, so recourse for harassment or assault is thin. The only documented official hostility—the 2005 port barring of an LGBTQ cruise, plus a 2011 statement—is dated, pre-decriminalisation and sexuality-focused, so it is a past signal not proof of current practice. Absence of trans violence, acceptance and enforcement data is not evidence of safety; the structural signals extrapolate to tier-3 hostility with thin recourse, in the Elevated Risk band.
